identification.summary: Periwinkle Tempest (formerly DEV-0193) is what Microsoft calls a financially motivated cybercriminal group. It develops, distributes and manages several payloads, including Trickbot, BazaLoader and AnchorDNS [S1][S2]. Microsoft describes it as the most prolific ransomware-associated cybercriminal activity group it tracked. It managed the Ryuk ransomware-as-a-service program until Ryuk shut down in June 2021 and also managed Ryuk's successor, Conti, as well as Diavol [S1][S2]. As other malware operations shut down, the group hired developers from Emotet, Qakbot and IcedID [S1][S2]. Microsoft also tracks DEV-0365, which provides Cobalt Strike Beacon infrastructure as a service to other cybercriminals, as a subgroup of DEV-0193 [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft has tracked DEV-0193 since October 2020 [S1][S2]. Per DOJ charges reported by TRM Labs, the Trickbot conspiracy began in November 2015 [S7].
identification.notes: Microsoft also associates the name 'Trickbot LLC' with this group [S1][S2]. Microsoft said DEV-0193 overlaps with activity Mandiant tracks as UNC1878 [S3]. Mandiant later promoted UNC1878 to FIN12, a Ryuk-deploying intrusion actor that 'worked closely with TrickBot-affiliated actors' [S10]. FIN12 is therefore best treated as a closely linked affiliate cluster, not a synonym for the Trickbot developers. German BKA reporting refers to the Trickbot group as 'Wizard Spider' [S9]. Microsoft's mapping places some Wizard Spider and Conti names under separate entries (Storm-0230, Conti Team 1, and Pistachio Tempest/DEV-0237, a Ryuk and Conti affiliate) [S2], so these boundaries should not be merged.

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor is assessed. Microsoft classifies Periwinkle Tempest as financially motivated [S1]. The US and UK governments describe the Trickbot group as Russia-based [S7].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft attributes the Trickbot, BazaLoader, AnchorDNS, Ryuk, Conti and Diavol management roles to DEV-0193/Periwinkle Tempest based on its telemetry and says leaked Conti chats from February 2022 confirmed the scale of the activity [S2]. The US and UK sanctioned alleged members in February and September 2023, and DOJ unsealed indictments of nine Russian nationals in September 2023 [S7]. In 2025 Germany's BKA publicly named a suspected founder and leader known as 'Stern' [S9].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and the Conti chat leak [S1][S2]; Microsoft's 2020 civil and technical action against Trickbot infrastructure [S4]; US Treasury and UK sanctions and DOJ indictments (via secondary coverage) [S7]; and the BKA's Operation Endgame identification (via secondary coverage) [S9].

objectives: Financial gain. The group runs malware and ransomware services that enable ransomware extortion of large organizations, and earlier ran banking and credential theft [S1][S2][S7]. According to DOJ charges as reported by TRM Labs, Trickbot was used to steal money and personal information [S7].

sectors: National government institutions, e.g. Costa Rica's finance and customs systems (Conti) [S8]
regions: Global, opportunistic (inferred from RaaS and botnet model; not region-limited in Microsoft reporting) [S1][S2]
targeting.notes: Microsoft's profile lists education and healthcare [S1]. Treasury said the group targeted many US critical infrastructure and health care providers during the COVID-19 pandemic [S7]. A joint CISA/FBI/HHS advisory warned of an imminent Trickbot and Ryuk threat to US hospitals in October 2020 [S5]. Mandiant found that nearly 20% of directly observed FIN12 victims were in healthcare [S10], but FIN12 is a separate, affiliated cluster.

capabilities.summary: The group develops and operates modular malware and loaders (Trickbot, BazaLoader, AnchorDNS) and manages ransomware programs (Ryuk, Conti, Diavol) [S1][S2]. Its DEV-0365 subgroup provides Cobalt Strike Beacon command-and-control as a service [S2]. In the typical Trickbot/Ryuk chain described by CISA, FBI and HHS, a malicious email installs Emotet and/or Trickbot, Trickbot moves laterally, disables protections and steals data, and Ryuk then encrypts systems [S5]. In 2021 its infrastructure hosted BazaLoader and Trickbot payloads alongside oleObjects used in CVE-2021-40444 (MSHTML) exploitation [S3]. The group recruits talent from other malware operations (Emotet, Qakbot, IcedID) [S1][S2], and the BKA said the group had more than 100 members at times [S9]. MITRE ATT&CK tracks the broader Wizard Spider cluster as G0102 [S11].

attack.name: Name Resolution Poisoning and SMB Relay

campaigns.name: Trickbot banking and credential theft conspiracy begins
campaigns.summary: DOJ charges allege Russian nationals conspired to use Trickbot to steal money and personal information beginning in November 2015 (reported by TRM Labs) [S7].

campaigns.name: Microsoft-led Trickbot infrastructure disruption
campaigns.summary: Using a court order and technical action with partners including FS-ISAC and NTT, Microsoft moved to cut off Trickbot infrastructure so that operators could not start new infections or activate ransomware already dropped. Microsoft framed the action partly as protection for the US elections [S4].

campaigns.name: Trickbot/Ryuk threat to US hospitals (AA20-302A)
campaigns.summary: CISA, FBI and HHS warned of credible information about an increased and imminent cybercrime threat to US hospitals from Trickbot leading to Ryuk ransomware [S5].

campaigns.name: Ryuk RaaS shutdown; Conti and Diavol continue
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says Periwinkle Tempest managed the Ryuk RaaS program until its June 2021 shutdown and also managed Conti and Diavol [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: CVE-2021-40444 MSHTML exploitation infrastructure overlap
campaigns.summary: Microsoft found that some infrastructure hosting oleObjects used in the August 2021 MSHTML attacks also delivered BazaLoader and Trickbot payloads, which overlaps with DEV-0193 [S3].

campaigns.name: Conti chat leak
campaigns.summary: Leaked Conti chat files from February 2022 confirmed the scale of DEV-0193 activity, according to Microsoft [S2]. Coverage tied the leak to Conti's public support for Russia's invasion of Ukraine [S8].

campaigns.name: Conti attacks on Costa Rican government
campaigns.summary: The State Department tied Conti to attacks on Costa Rican government institutions that severely hampered tax and customs processing, and offered up to $10 million for information on Conti leaders [S8]. Microsoft last observed a Conti deployment on 19 April 2022 [S2].

campaigns.name: Second sanctions round and DOJ indictments
campaigns.summary: OFAC and the UK sanctioned eleven more individuals, and DOJ unsealed indictments of nine people tied to Trickbot and Conti (reported by TRM Labs) [S7].

campaigns.name: BKA names suspected Trickbot founder 'Stern' (Operation Endgame)
campaigns.summary: Germany's BKA named Vitaly Nikolaevich Kovalev, alias 'Stern', as the suspected founder of the Trickbot group, during an Operation Endgame round (reported by Heise) [S9].

diamond.adversary: A Russia-based, financially motivated criminal enterprise (Trickbot LLC) whose BKA-named suspected leader is 'Stern' [S1][S7][S9]. The BKA said it had more than 100 members at times [S9].
diamond.capability: Trickbot, BazaLoader, AnchorDNS, Ryuk, Conti, Diavol, and Cobalt Strike Beacon as a service [S1][S2]. Infrastructure overlapped with CVE-2021-40444 exploitation [S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Trickbot botnet C2, which Microsoft and partners targeted in 2020 [S4]. DEV-0365 Cobalt Strike C2-as-a-service [S2]. Infrastructure that hosted MSHTML exploit documents also delivered BazaLoader and Trickbot payloads [S3].
diamond.victim: Healthcare and public health, education, US critical infrastructure, and government institutions (Costa Rica) [S1][S5][S7][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Ransomware-as-a-service gig economy relationships with affiliates and access brokers [S2]. Members operate from Russia beyond Western arrest [S9]. Pro-Russia stance by Conti in 2022 triggered an insider leak [S8].
diamond.technology: Windows enterprise networks reached via malicious email, commodity loaders and lateral movement before encryption [S5]. Microsoft Office/MSHTML exploitation (CVE-2021-40444) [S3].

gaps: Microsoft's current mapping splits Wizard Spider/Conti names across Periwinkle Tempest, Storm-0230 and Pistachio Tempest; how much of MITRE G0102 activity belongs to Periwinkle Tempest specifically is unresolved.

Primary US government documents (Treasury press releases, DOJ indictments, the CISA advisory page, the State Department reward notice) could not be opened; facts rely on secondary coverage or AHA's copy.
BKA primary statement not reviewed; the exact date of the Kovalev/Stern announcement (late May 2025) is unverified.
No sourced reporting found on Periwinkle Tempest-branded activity after 2024 (e.g., successor ransomware brands, current loaders).
FIN12/UNC1878 overlap: Microsoft says DEV-0193 overlaps UNC1878 [S3], but Mandiant treats FIN12 as a Ryuk-deploying affiliate; the precise relationship is unclear.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1 (operational environment): Treat the defense industrial base, base hospitals and medical treatment facilities, and education and training enclaves on commercial or DODIN-adjacent networks as in scope, since the group has hit healthcare, education and critical infrastructure [S1][S5][S7]. Step 2 (effects): Ransomware encryption of Windows enterprise systems can degrade medical, logistics and administrative mission support, and the Costa Rica case shows national government services can be disrupted [S5][S8]. Step 3 (adversary model): Email-delivered loaders (Emotet/Trickbot/BazaLoader) lead to Cobalt Strike, then lateral movement, then data theft, then Ryuk/Conti-family encryption. Access is often shared or sold to affiliates [S2][S5]. Step 4 (courses of action): The most likely course of action is opportunistic loader infection of a mission-partner or support network, followed by affiliate ransomware within days. The most dangerous is a time-sensitive ransomware event against healthcare or a critical-infrastructure dependency (power, water, comms supporting an installation) during a crisis or surge, timed for maximum leverage, as with the 2020 hospital threat [S5][S7]. Candidate indicators: Trickbot/BazaLoader/AnchorDNS artifacts; Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 matching DEV-0365 patterns; malicious Office documents exploiting MSHTML; and protection tampering before encryption [S2][S3][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: Fuse Microsoft, CISA/FBI and vendor indicators for Trickbot-lineage loaders and Cobalt Strike-as-a-service infrastructure into DODIN and mission-partner monitoring [S2][S3][S5]. Authorities: This is a criminal actor, so the primary responses are law enforcement (DOJ indictments, BKA/Operation Endgame), sanctions (OFAC/UK) and private civil action (Microsoft's 2020 court order) [S4][S7][S9]. Any DoD role should be coordinated through those lanes and existing defense-support authorities. Mission assurance: Prioritize backup integrity and recovery for medical and logistics systems and plan for loss of supporting civilian infrastructure, given healthcare and critical-infrastructure targeting [S5][S7]. Coordination: Coordinate with CISA, FBI, HHS (for medical facilities) and allied partners such as the UK and Germany, who have acted jointly against the group [S5][S7][S9].

provenance.importedSummary: GRIM SPIDER is a sophisticated eCrime group that has been operating the Ryuk ransomware since August 2018, targeting large organizations for a high-ransom return. This methodology, known as “big game hunting,” signals a shift in operations for WIZARD SPIDER, a criminal enterprise of which GRIM SPIDER appears to be a cell. The WIZARD SPIDER threat group, known as the Russia-based operator of the TrickBot banking malware, had focused primarily on wire fraud in the past. Similar to Samas and BitPaymer, Ryuk is specifically used to target enterprise environments. Code comparison between versions of Ryuk and Hermes ransomware indicates that Ryuk was derived from the Hermes source code and has been under steady development since its release. Hermes is commodity ransomware that has been observed for sale on forums and used by multiple threat actors. However, Ryuk is only used by GRIM SPIDER and, unlike Hermes, Ryuk has only been used to target enterprise environments. Since Ryuk’s appearance in August, the threat actors operating it have netted over 705.80 BTC across 52 transactions for a total current value of $3,701,893.98 USD. Grim Spider is reportedly associated with Lunar Spider and Wizard Spider.
